question: I got a call from someone saying they're from RBI and my KYC is expired, asking me to transfer money to a new account to reactivate my banking. Is this true?
reference_answer: RBI does not ask individuals to deposit money into personal accounts or share KYC details, OTPs, or passwords; you should immediately contact your bank branch and ignore such calls.

steps.text: If you have already lost money, report the fraud immediately to the cyber crime helpline number 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in.
Do not share account login credentials, card information, PINs, passwords, OTPs with anyone.
Do not share KYC documents or copies of KYC documents with unknown or unidentified individuals or organizations.
Do not click on suspicious or unverified links received in mobile or email.

Beware of calls, emails, and any other communication by cybercriminals posing as officials from Government agencies/ RBI, asking for transfer of money under the pretext of any enticing offer or alarming issue.

question: I shared my bank OTP with a scammer and money was taken from my account. Do I have to pay back the full amount, or will the bank cover some of it?
reference_answer: If the loss occurred because you shared your payment details, you are responsible for the full amount until you report the incident to the bank. After you report it, the bank bears any further loss.

steps.text: Notify your bank immediately about the fraudulent transaction.
Take acknowledgement from your bank when you notify them of the complaint.
The bank must resolve your complaint within 90 days from the date of receipt.
If fraudulent transactions continue even after you have informed the bank, the bank will have to bear the loss.
Report the incident through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (www.cybercrime.gov.in) or call the dedicated cybercrime helpline number 1930 for immediate assistance.

question: I saw an unauthorized deduction from my bank account. What are my chances of getting my money back, and how quickly do I need to act?
reference_answer: Reporting the unauthorized transaction within 3 working days of the bank's communication may give you zero liability for third-party faults, while reporting within 4 to 7 working days limits your loss to ₹5,000 or ₹10,000 depending on your account type. If you were negligent (e.g., shared credentials), you are responsible for the loss until you report it, after which the bank covers any further transactions.

steps.text: Notify your bank immediately about the unauthorized transaction and take an acknowledgement from the bank.
If you inform the bank within 3 working days of the unauthorized transaction and there is no customer negligence, you have no liability for the loss.
If the fraudulent transactions continue even after you have informed the bank, the bank must reimburse those amounts.
The bank has to resolve your complaint within 90 days from the date of receipt.
If loss is due to negligence of the customer (sharing password etc.) then customer will bear the loss till the bank is informed.
Report the fraud through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (www.cybercrime.gov.in) or call the dedicated cybercrime helpline number 1930 for immediate assistance.
